group_structure: Global bank with three client segments (Corporate & Investment Banking, Wealth & Retail Banking, Ventures). The UAE is one of the group's ten disclosed 'key markets' and Dubai is described as the regional hub for Africa and the Middle East and home of the global Islamic banking arm, Standard Chartered Saadiq. In the DIFC the bank operates as Standard Chartered Bank (DIFC Branch), DFSA-licensed since 2004 (deposits, credit, advising, arranging, dealing, custody, fund administration, trust services; Islamic window). In Saudi Arabia it operates a branch led by a country CEO and owns Standard Chartered Capital (Saudi Arabia) (100%). SC Ventures (innovation/venture arm) announced an ADGM office in Jan 2024. All figures in this file labelled 'Group (global)' cover the whole group; UAE figures are the group's management-basis key-market disclosure, not standalone audited UAE accounts.

people.name: Maria Ramos
people.title: Group Chair
people.appointed_note: Appointed Group Chair in May 2025, succeeding Jose Vinals (S33, S3). Independent non-executive director and member of the Court of Standard Chartered Bank since January 2021; Senior Independent Director from September 2022 until she became Group Chair (S33).
people.previous_roles: May 2025- Group Chair, Standard Chartered PLC (Chair, Governance and Nomination Committee); Sep 2022-May 2025 Senior Independent Director; Jan 2021- independent non-executive director, Standard Chartered PLC, and member of the Court of Standard Chartered Bank; 2009-2019 Chief Executive Officer, ABSA Group Limited (formerly Barclays Africa Group); before ABSA, five years as group chief executive of Transnet Ltd; before that seven years as director-general of South Africa's National Treasury; non-executive director of the Saudi British Bank and the Public Investment Corporation until Dec 2020 (S3); Chair, AngloGold Ashanti PLC until May 2024; non-executive director, Compagnie Financiere Richemont SA until March 2025; earlier boards: Sanlam Ltd, Remgro Ltd, SABMiller plc. Current other roles: Member, Group of Thirty; International Advisory Board member, Blavatnik School of Government, Oxford University; Advisory board member, Wits Foundation Board of Governors; Board member, Institute of International Finance; Member, Leadership Council of TheCityUK; Member, National Financial Regulatory Administration International Advisory Council; Member, High-Level Private Sector Advisory Group, Asian Development Bank (S33).
people.role_evidence: Official Board of Directors page and profile checked 2026-10-13 (S5, S33); AR 2025 director biography ('Group Chair in May 2025', S3). A 2026-10-13 news search found no departure or successor.

capabilities.wealth_summary: In the UAE, Standard Chartered runs a tiered wealth franchise (Premium, Priority from AED 370k average balance, Priority Private for HNW, International banking, and Global Private Bank) led by Rajesh Kannan (Wealth & Retail Banking UAE) and Ayesha Abbas (Affluent and Wealth Solutions, EMEA & UAE) under regional CEO Rola Abu Manneh. It opened its first Priority Private centre in Europe, Middle East and Africa in Dubai in Feb 2025, and the Private Bank expanded its UAE frontline team 20% by end-2024 and made further UAE hires in May 2025. The shelf includes 100+ online mutual funds, house Signature CIO Funds and Signature Select VCC funds (an APAC multi-asset fund sub-managed by BlackRock was launched to UAE Priority/Priority Private/Private clients in Jul 2026), fixed income, hedge funds for Professional Investors, wealth lending, and SC Mobile online equity trading in 40,000+ stocks and ETFs on 10 global exchanges. The DIFC branch is DFSA-licensed for advising, dealing, custody (incl. crypto tokens) and trust services. Group affluent AUM was USD 447bn at end-2025; no UAE/GCC AUM is disclosed.

House funds (Signature CIO Funds; Signature Select funds under the group's VCC platform, with external sub-managers such as BlackRock) are distributed in the UAE; group says combined AUM of SC exclusive funds exceeded USD 8bn (2025, global).

brokerage.detail: Online Equity Trading via SC Mobile/Online Banking: 40,000+ stocks and ETFs on 10 exchanges (5 US venues, SIX Swiss, Singapore, Hong Kong, Tokyo, ASX); no UAE/GCC exchanges listed; no third-party broker named.

digital_investing.detail: SC Mobile app/Online Banking: online equity and ETF trading, online mutual funds (100+), Trade FX, myRM (relationship-manager channel in app), SC Digiadvisory. Launch dates not stated.

advisory.detail: Investment specialists and RMs; SC Wealth Select advisory approach; SC-INSEAD Wealth Academy-trained advisers for Priority Private; DIFC branch licensed for advising on financial products.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Signature CIO Funds are described as 'foundational portfolios' (fund-based); no robo-advice or model-portfolio service found for the UAE.

funds_platform.detail: 100+ funds available online; interactive funds library; fund houses not named on the UAE page.

structured_products.detail: DFSA licence of the DIFC branch covers structured products (advising, arranging, dealing); not mentioned on UAE retail investment pages.

private_markets.detail: Hedge funds (alternative investments) offered to Professional Investors; Signature Select fund includes liquid alternatives; no private-markets offering found for the UAE.

islamic_wealth.detail: Standard Chartered Saadiq (global Islamic arm, based in Dubai) offers Shariah-compliant accounts, term deposits, cards and home finance in the UAE; no Shariah-compliant investment products found on UAE investment pages. DIFC branch has an Islamic window endorsement.

initiatives.what: Launched Signature Select APAC Allocation Plus (VCC sub-fund, BlackRock sub-manager) to Accredited/Professional Investors in UAE Priority, Priority Private and Private Banking; eighth VCC sub-fund since Jun 2024.
During regional conflict, extended remote working for Dubai teams while keeping UAE services running (CEO statement).
SC Ventures said at Money20/20 Riyadh it plans to raise a USD 250m digital-asset fund in 2026 targeting Middle East investors.
Global Private Bank added senior UAE hires (EMEA market head, GCC UHNW lead, RMs); group plans to invest USD 1.5bn in the Affluent business over five years.
Opened first Priority Private centre in Europe, Middle East and Africa in Dubai, with corridor rooms for Africa, India, China, Singapore and Jersey/UK.
SC Ventures announced an office in ADGM, Abu Dhabi, led by Gautam Jain.

opportunities: UAE online trading covers only international exchanges (US, Swiss, Asian, ASX), with no UAE/GCC markets listed (S16).
No discretionary or model-portfolio service found on UAE pages; the DIFC licence has no managing-assets permission (S15, S19).
Group is investing USD 1.5bn in Affluent over five years and is expanding its UAE private bank (S12); affluent NNM was USD 33bn in H1 2026 (S1).
Private markets are not evident in the UAE shelf; alternatives limited to hedge funds for Professional Investors (S18).
barriers: Global bank with group-built platforms (SC Mobile, myRM, SC Wealth Select) and own house-fund range (Signature CIO / Signature Select VCC), so product and platform decisions are likely taken at group level (S15, S17, S21).
Existing product partnership with BlackRock for house multi-asset funds (S21).
Has its own venture arm (SC Ventures) building fintechs, with an ADGM presence (S9, S25).

open_items: Internal-note contact 'Rola Aboumanny, Head of RCO' could not be matched to a public title; confirm internally whether this was Rola Abu Manneh (CEO UAE, ME & Pakistan) or another person.

No official UAE/Middle East leadership page on sc.com/ae (the About us and CEO-message pages carry no leadership list); regional roles are verified from press releases, news and LinkedIn snippets only. Neither sc.com nor the Annual Report 2025 publishes degrees for Group executives, so education is empty for them.
Priority Private eligibility not opened (programme T&Cs PDF); press says USD 1m-10m.
Group major shareholders not checked (not needed for GCC scope).

LinkedIn: role-based searches on 2026-10-13 (Saudi CEO, Global Private Bank EMEA, SC Ventures Abu Dhabi) found no profile URL for Mazen Bunyan, Sarah Al Khelaiwi, Yahya Ismail or Gautam Jain. A result 'Alex Manson - SC Ventures by Standard Chartered' (sg.linkedin.com/in/alex-manson-919a8310a) shows no title, so it was not recorded. No LinkedIn search was run for Ramos, Winters, Hsu or Hoornweg.

Bahrain, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait: sc.com/bh shows a Bahrain retail bank with 4 branches (CBB-licensed) but no leadership page, and no current country CEO for Bahrain, Qatar or Oman was found; the only country-CEO appointments found are in an SC release (undated on the page; changes effective by 31 Mar 2019) at https://www.sc.com/en/press-release/weve-announced-key-appointments-in-the-middle-east/, too old to record. No country head for these markets is profiled.

Possible later holder of a similar role: a LinkedIn snippet for a 'Huda Saif' shows 'Head of Affluent & Wealth, EMEA and UAE' at SC (search result only, not verified); Ayesha Abbas was quoted with the senior title in Jul 2026.

Leads from 2026-10-13 LinkedIn role searches, not recorded and not verified: a result lists Momin Jaffar as 'Managing Director & Group Head, Standard Chartered Global Private Bank' (Dubai International Financial Centre, Sept 2026 event listing); another says Ali Raza joined as Cluster Head for the Middle East and Africa in Global Private Bank, Dubai (no date). The official May 2026 investor bios name Raymond Ang as Global Head, Private Bank and Affluent Clients (S32), an Asia-based global role not profiled. Check these against an official source before adding.

Global Private Bank people (Gandhi, Ismail, Haddad) and SC Ventures' Gautam Jain rest on a May 2025 official release, a Jan 2024 / Sep 2025 / Jul 2025 trade report and a DFSA register entry; no 2026 official page confirms their titles, so they stay 'Requires verification'.
Standard Chartered DIFC's Senior Executive Officer is named in the 3 Sep 2026 release (S36) but is not profiled (not a wealth, digital or country-CEO role).
UAE legal entity form (subsidiary vs branch) unresolved; see discrepancies.
